hypothesis:
Mechanism: Anchor-Relative Log-Distance Primal-Dual Loop (ALD-PDL) replaces the additive correction cap with a cumulative log(target-distance / anchor-distance) primal state, while the recurrent dual state damps only increases in a source-train-defined log-energy and the same recalled pre-norm Transformer block remains tied for four loops.
Hypothesis: GLPDT already halves same-protocol source error and converges across loops, but its additive action space reaches only 6/12 validation endpoints; an anchor-relative log-distance action space preserves exact positivity and swap equivariance while allowing multiplicative contraction and expansion without a hand-tuned range cap.
Observable: On the unchanged 13/6 object-disjoint source B_dev, all 12 endpoint distances are representable, ALD-PDL lowers mean-side and worst-side NMAE versus node 8.14 and a parameter-matched one-loop control, exact swap error is <=1e-6, per-loop residual decreases, and target-relative p99 error does not regress versus frozen D2.
Conflicts: Validated [8.14] showed recurrent evidence accumulation works but its fixed additive cap leaves half the validation sides unreachable and yields prediction/anchor p99=32.8629; this node keeps the loop and changes the primal geometry rather than tuning the cap, seed, width, loop count, or split.
insight: Anchor-relative log-distance removes the additive action-space floor: representability rose from 6/12 to 12/12, mean-side NMAE improved 16.94% versus node8.14 and 60.85% versus D2, worst-side NMAE fell to 0.324730, and target-relative p99 fell from D2 3.4413 to 1.1823. However the same trained parameters at one loop score 0.258452, beating the four-loop final state, and the last prediction residual rises from 0.01225 to 0.02027, proving the remaining problem is recurrent overshoot/non-contractive fixed-point dynamics rather than action-space reachability.
